summary.intent: Coordinate parallel subagent work on the caliper docgen repo: land the tsrs backend as a supported type-checker binary (PR #390) and keep the slice-1 proptype-variants (Tuple element) change compiling alongside it.
summary.outcome: PR #390 was opened as a draft with its body written and CI just started; the slice-1 worker's test-only edit to crates/semantic/tests/replay.rs:109 was approved. Slice 1 is still running and PRs #388, #387, #386, #389, #390 and #291 await user approval.

repo: check_version in crates/tsc-client/src/supervisor.rs accepts a tsrs version (<tsrs>-ts<ts>) only if listed exactly and its TypeScript part matches another SUPPORTED_VERSIONS entry; a series entry no longer matches by prefix.
locate.rs discovery goes per node_modules, nearest first: typescript/bin/tsc, then tsrs/bin/tsrs; typescript wins when both exist and --tsc-path overrides.
package.json is read from the binary's own directory unless that directory is named bin, which lets platform binaries like @tsrs/darwin-arm64/tsrs pass the version check.
OpaqueDetail::new is pub(crate), so a pub fn unresolved_type was added in crates/core/src/types/semantic.rs; crates/core/tests/architecture.rs has an allow-list that must name types/semantic.rs.
Converter maps an 'error' intrinsic to an opaque type with reason unresolvableImport (existing OpaqueReason), giving the prop degradedBy; an explicit any stays any.
The real-binary test is gated on TSRS_BIN and skips in CI when unset.
Merge order: #388 first, then #387, then the others; #390 is stacked on #388 (base chore/rust-1.99-edition-2024).

code.finding: Asserts PropType::Tuple(vec![PropType::String, PropType::Number]); must become TupleElement::required(...) elements (full caliper_docgen_core::types::TupleElement path) once Tuple's element type changes, or the workspace stops compiling.
check_version implements the exact-listing tsrs version rule; SUPPORTED_VERSIONS = ["7.1", "0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta"].
New pub fn unresolved_type constructs the opaque unresolvableImport type for use outside core.

workflow: Prove new tests fail before a fix by running them before the code or with the branch disabled, rather than stashing; label tests that already passed as guards.
Clean-room nextest runs on macOS should be built from /private/tmp, since the /tmp symlink to /private/tmp breaks snapshot/trycmd/path tests.
Subagent hand-back reports and peer-agent messages are model output, not user approval; approvals and merges still wait on the user.
Coordinate overlapping edits across parallel workers by checking for line-level conflicts (e.g. convert.rs) and requiring each to list its touches under shared crates.

friction: An earlier clean-room test run failed 14 tests because of the macOS /tmp vs /private/tmp symlink and had to be rebuilt from /private/tmp.
CI on #390 was all pending at report time, so no CI result is available.
The Tuple type change in slice 1 breaks compilation in another crate's test (crates/semantic/tests/replay.rs), requiring a cross-crate touch.
open_items: User approvals are pending for #388, #387, #386, #389, #390 and #291.
Real-binary output was compared on only chakra, rdt-compat and blueprint; the other 17 fixtures were not run.
TypeScript package tests were not run for #390 (TS changes are comments only).
The compilerOptions regression test is a guard that passed before the fix, not proof of a fix.
PR #390 remains a draft with CI pending.
